# Troubleshooting (v2)

Diagnose common Uniswap v2 integration errors, including K, rebasing edge cases, and router transaction failures.

This page covers error codes and failure patterns frequently encountered while integrating with Uniswap v2.

## [UniswapV2: K](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#uniswapv2-k)

`K` errors happen when a swap attempt leaves pair reserves below invariant expectations.

## [Fee On Transfer Tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#fee-on-transfer-tokens)

### [Inclusive fee-on-transfer tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#inclusive-fee-on-transfer-tokens)

These tokens burn or divert part of each transfer, so the recipient receives less than the sender transfers.

Use router functions ending in `SupportingFeeOnTransfer` to validate output amounts on receipt.

### [Exclusive fee-on-transfer tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#exclusive-fee-on-transfer-tokens)

These tokens send an additional trailing transfer after the primary transfer.

Because the router cannot anticipate that trailing transfer, swaps may revert or leave pair state inconsistent.

## [Rebasing Tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#rebasing-tokens)

Rebasing tokens can change balances independently of transfers, which can create reserve drift.

### [Negative rebasing tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#negative-rebasing-tokens)

Negative rebases can unbalance pool reserves and shift losses to the next transacting account.

### [Positive rebasing tokens](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#positive-rebasing-tokens)

Positive rebases can create surplus balances that are not reflected in reserve accounting. Third parties may capture this surplus via `skim()`.

### [Notes on rebasing support](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#notes-on-rebasing-support)

If you are designing rebasing tokens, account for integration behavior explicitly. Wrapper patterns such as [CHAI](https://chai.money/about.html) can improve compatibility.

## [Router and Transaction Errors](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#router-and-transaction-errors)

### [UniswapV2: LOCKED](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#uniswapv2-locked)

`LOCKED` is the router reentrancy guard.

### [No Access To Archive Node](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#no-access-to-archive-node)

This is usually an environment issue with local fork tooling.

### [UniswapV2: TRANSFER\_FAILED](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#uniswapv2-transfer_failed)

The core contract could not transfer tokens to the recipient.

### [UniswapV2: EXPIRED](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#uniswapv2-expired)

The transaction deadline elapsed before inclusion onchain.

### [Action Requires an Active Reserve](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#action-requires-an-active-reserve)

`VM Exception While Processing Transaction: Action Requires an Active Reserve`

### [Unable To Approve Transaction On The Front End](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/troubleshooting\#unable-to-approve-transaction-on-the-front-end)

Some tokens block direct allowance increases. Setting allowance to zero first, then setting the target amount, usually resolves this.
